newsitem.title: UK: London gold holds on but negative thinking grows.
newsitem.headline: London gold holds on but negative thinking grows.

text.p: Gold prices tottered on the verge of 20-month lows after the bearish sentiment of last week swept through the markets again on Monday.
Playing on already fraying nerves, dealers added, was what they called an increasingly loud whisper that a central bank had sold bullion into the market.
New York reopened after its two-day Thanksgiving holiday marked down over $2.00 per ounce as forecast.
By then short covering against the U.S. price holding meant London was slightly above morning levels.
"It's vulnerable longer term though. The mood is pretty negative," one dealer said.

Selling by South African and Australian gold miners as they became increasingly anxious to protect their income against falling prices was also cited as a major factor eroding the value of gold and the market's confidence.
"There has been a continual drip of metal on the market. It's been disappointing that the price is at a 20-month low at a time when it is traditionally high," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $370.75 per ounce after $370.50 on Monday and $371.30 on Friday, putting the market's current value a matter of pennies above its fixing on April 25, 1994 at $370.25.
A market analyst said, "Any rally will be sold into. As a senior dealer told me, "Sell now before the Christmas rush!'"
The spot gold price was around $373.50 when the U.S. markets finished for their break last Wednesday.
Dealers and analysts cited a string of clues to the presence of a central bank in the market including rising lease rates and isolated big offerings on the fixings.

Also significantly undermining confidence was the absence of physical buying. "There was good physical demand at around $375.00. Now the buyers seem to be waiting for lower prices," another dealer said.
Dealers said that could mean a fall to $365 or even lower before the buyers come back in numbers.

Of the gold producers' maneouvring, a dealer said, "If you look at the Australian dollar (price), it's down to A$451. Producers are going to have to sell the stuff and the further down the gold price goes the more pressure is on them."
The other precious metals were at best steady. Platinum was at $373.65/$364.65, down $0.35, silver just a cent above key key support at $4.71/$4.73 and Palladium was unchanged at $114.25/$115.25.
